For metrics still MISSING after the rules: the LLM PROPOSES a line, the validator DECIDES. Off by default — a model error never fails the run.

fill_missing(observations, raw_by_statement, …)
1. Baseline validate with rules only. Chooser None → return unchanged.
2. Show the LLM the numbered lines of the located page, ask ONE
question per MISSING metric: "which line is this?" (build_prompt).
3. Prune loop: drop any proposal not VERIFIED by a check involving a
rule value — repeat until stable (removing one can unverify others).
4. Safety veto: if the kept set would newly FLAG a rule value, drop ALL.
5. Accept survivors as VERIFIED with source "llm".
_proven_by_rules: two LLM picks agreeing only with each other don't count
Providers (one-method interface)
GeminiChooser
gemini-2.5-flash, JSON response schema, temp 0.
GroqChooser
llama-3.3-70b, json_object response, temp 0.
chooser_from_env()
FINAGENT_LLM_PROVIDER = gemini | groq
+ GEMINI_API_KEY / GROQ_API_KEY
unset → None → fallback off, pipeline unchanged
Five guarantees, not hopes
• The LLM returns a line id, never a figure — the value is read off the page by the same parser the rules use. It cannot invent a number.
• A wrong line is caught by the accounting identities — a proposal is accepted only if a check including a rule-extracted value verifies it.
• A proposal must not break anything — if adding it would FLAG a value the rules already found, it is dropped.
• Every accepted value shows source "llm" — an unchecked LLM value is never shown, not even as PROBABLE.
• Off by default — no provider configured behaves exactly as before; any LLM error leaves the metric MISSING and the run succeeds.
the design principle: the LLM widens recall, the validator guards precision — the model can only ever help, never corrupt.
